title: Rate Limiter
subtitle: A simple counter lets double the limit through at the window edge, and a token bucket does not
motto: Say no early, say it fairly, and say it in one place
keyInsight: How you count matters: a fixed window can pass twice the limit across its boundary, while a token bucket allows a bounded burst and holds the average.

decisions.title: Show the boundary burst on purpose
decisions.description: The failure frame sends the same bursts at 0.9 s and 1.0 s, straddling a window edge, because that is the exact case the simple counter gets wrong.
decisions.alternatives: Testing only well-timed traffic would make the fixed window look correct.

decisions.title: Measure the worst 100 ms, not the average
decisions.description: The metric is the biggest burst let through, since the backend fails on bursts, not on per-second averages.
decisions.alternatives: Counting requests per second would show 20 for both algorithms and hide the difference.
